sense: the same in size, number or value

terms.gloss: equal, a match for; even (of numbers)
terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; with a dative or cum
evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.49: jūra certē paria dēbent esse
Cic. Sen. 7: parēs … cum paribus facillimē congregantur
terms.comment: Equal in size, number, strength or rank, and so a match for someone: verbum Latīnum pār Graecō (Cic. Fin. 2.12, Lewis & Short). Pār impār is the game of odd or even (Hor. S. 2.3.248). Its neuter noun is a pair (see pair).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.30: quod dubitēs aequum sit an inīquum
terms.comment: Its first sense is level, flat (aequus locus); then equal, of shares, distances and terms; and above all fair, reasonable (aequum est, it is right) and calm (aequō animō) (Lewis & Short). For equal in size or number pār is the plainer word.

terms.gloss: equal, like; of the same age
evidence: Cic. Or. 188: partem pedis aut aequālem esse alterī partī
Cic. Sen. 10: ut aequālem, like a man of my own age (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Most often “of the same age”, “contemporary” (aequālis meus, Ter., Cic.); as “equal” it is a word of measures and parts.

phrases.latin: sī ingenia omnium paria esse nōn possunt, jūra certē paria dēbent esse eōrum inter sē, quī sunt cīvēs in eādem rē pūblicā
phrases.english: if everyone’s talents cannot be equal, the rights of those who are citizens of the same state should at least be equal among themselves

phrases.latin: parēs autem vetere prōverbiō cum paribus facillimē congregantur
phrases.english: and equals, as the old proverb says, flock together most easily with equals
